key_insight: A high-throughput DFT search found 58 CuI-based ternary compounds with promising p-type transparent-conductor behavior, and showed that CuI halides can follow generalized CMVB rules beyond traditional oxide delafossites.
engineering_relevance: This expands the design space for transparent p-type contacts and electrode materials that could improve tandem photovoltaics and transparent electronics.
method: Used minima hopping to explore X–Cu–I compound structures.
Applied DFT-based screening for thermodynamic stability, optical transparency, and light hole effective mass.
Revisited chemical modulation of the valence band (CMVB) descriptors to extract transferable design rules.
evidence_signal: The screening identified 58 candidates, including 49 previously unreported compounds and 20 degenerate p-type semiconductors; Cu2FI2 was highlighted with a 3.75 eV gap and 0.262 m0 hole effective mass.
watch_item: The findings are computational predictions, so experimental synthesis, defect control, and carrier mobility will need validation before device integration.
paper_title: High-throughput computational discovery of CuI-based ternary $p$-type transparent conductors
